candidate_rule.strategy_name: Category-benchmark deviation: DRIV vs. "Miscellaneous Sector" major-tier peers
candidate_rule.hypothesis: DRIV is statistically likely to converge back toward the return of its "Miscellaneous Sector" category's major-issuer peers after diverging by an unusual amount.
candidate_rule.rule_summary: Trade DRIV against the equal-weight return of its category's major-tier peers (FAN, ICLN, TAN): go long DRIV when its z-score deviation falls to -1.5, exit back to cash once it recovers to -0.25.
candidate_rule.asset_eligibility_logic: Requires point-in-time history for DRIV and all of FAN, ICLN, TAN covering at least 20 trading days at every rebalance.
candidate_rule.signal_logic: Daily z-score of the return spread between DRIV and the equal-weight return of its major-tier category peers, over a trailing 20-day rolling window.
candidate_rule.position_logic: Single position: fully allocate to the long leg when in the trade, fully in cash otherwise. No shorting; max gross leverage 1.0x.
candidate_rule.entry_logic: Enter when the spread z-score falls to or below -1.5.
candidate_rule.exit_logic: Exit when the spread z-score rises back to or above -0.25.
candidate_rule.rebalancing_logic: Rebalances only when the entry/exit condition changes; otherwise holds the current position unchanged.

specialty_evidence_usage.fundamental_trader.category_scan.DRIV: Category-benchmark correlation and deviation z-score evidence used to select this ticker and its lookback window.

constraint_handling: Long-only, single-ticker, unlevered - stays within a research-stage mandate's default risk footprint.
implementation_notes: DRIV (Global X Funds, boutique tier) has diverged +1.56 std from its "Miscellaneous Sector" category benchmark (FAN, ICLN, TAN, major tier) over the trailing 20 trading days, with 0.73 return correlation to that benchmark historically.
Category benchmark is an in-house equal-weight average of major-tier issuer peers in the same ETF_info.xlsx category, not a licensed index.
ISSUER_SCALE_TIER (major vs. boutique fund family) substitutes for expense ratio / dividend yield / NAV premium-discount, which are not populated in this fixture.

specialty_evidence_usage.quant_trader.pair_scan.IGV_JEPQ: Correlation and AR(1) mean-reversion half-life evidence used to select this pair and size its lookback window.

constraint_handling: Long-only, single-pair, unlevered - stays within a research-stage mandate's default risk footprint.
implementation_notes: IGV and JEPQ moved together closely during the training window (correlation 0.8903 over 278 shared trading days), and their price spread snapped back toward its average in about 7.89 trading days. That combination - a real relationship plus a measurable pull back to normal - is what makes this a testable mean-reversion anomaly. Trade the spread: buy IGV when it is cheap versus JEPQ by 1.5 standard deviations, exit as the gap closes back to 0.25 standard deviations.
